- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast to reflect risk of rebound.
- After sharp price spikes, model frequently overshoots in next period; apply downward correction by 5–10% of spike magnitude.
- If 3–5 consecutive forecast days show upward trend but true outcome reverses, model exhibits mean reversion bias; adjust downward in next period.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-stage momentum; add 1–2% lagged sentiment-weighted adjustment to final forecast.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
